questions.stem: A 26-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks is admitted in spontaneous labour. Four hours later the cardiotocograph shows recurrent late decelerations with reduced variability.

parts.label: a)
parts.text: List the causes of this cardiotocograph pattern.

subparts.label: c.i)
subparts.text: State the factors that decide the mode of delivery.

subparts.label: c.ii)
subparts.text: Describe the preparation for an emergency caesarean section.

keyLearningPoints: Intrauterine resuscitation comes before delivery is decided.
Mode of delivery depends on cervical dilatation, station and how fast the fetus is deteriorating.
questions.modelAnswer:
**a)** Uteroplacental insufficiency from maternal hypotension (often after regional analgesia), uterine hyperstimulation, placental abruption, maternal hypoxia…

**b)** Stop oxytocin, left lateral position, intravenous fluids, oxygen if hypoxic, consider tocolysis, vaginal examination to assess progress…

**c)** …

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman presents with heavy menstrual bleeding for one year. Her haemoglobin is 8.4 g/dL.

parts.label: a)
parts.text: Describe how you would evaluate her.

parts.label: b)
parts.text: Discuss the medical options for treatment.

keyLearningPoints: Exclude endometrial pathology at this age before treating empirically.
The levonorgestrel intrauterine system is first-line medical treatment.
